🤿 Deep dive · Lesson 10 · 2 min read

Creative AI

How AI makes pictures, music and stories, how a picture appears out of noise, and the questions it raises.

Learning patterns, making something new

Generative AI learns from huge numbers of examples: millions of pictures with their captions, thousands of hours of music, mountains of text. It doesn't keep a copy of every example to paste back later. Instead, it learns their patterns: what cats look like, how a pop song is built, which words tend to follow which. Then it uses those patterns to make something new, like “a cat astronaut in watercolour”: a picture that never existed before. The same idea works for stories, music, voices and short videos.

From noise to picture

Many of today's image generators are diffusion models. In training, the model sees pictures with more and more random noise added, like the static on an old TV, until nothing is left but noise. Its job is to learn the way back: to guess which part of a noisy picture is noise, so that it can be taken away. To make a new picture, it starts from pure random noise and removes it step by step. Your prompt guides every step, so the shapes that appear are the ones you asked for. Start from different noise, and the same prompt gives a different picture.

Did you know? An earlier idea, from 2014, is the GAN (generative adversarial network). Two networks compete: one, like a forger, makes fake pictures; the other, like a detective, tries to tell them from real ones. Each one makes the other better. GANs became famous for photos of faces of people who never existed.

A creative partner

A good prompt says what you want, in what style and mood, with the details that matter. Then you edit: change one thing at a time, ask for variations, keep the best and improve it. Used like this, AI is a creative partner. It can help you brainstorm ideas, sketch a poster, make a background for your game or try out a beat. But the choices are yours: what to make, what to keep, what to change. And when you show work that AI helped with, say so.

Did you know? Build a picture prompt in layers: the subject (“a fox”), a style (“paper cut-out”), the light or mood (“at sunset”), then the details (“wearing a red scarf”). Change one layer at a time and compare the results: you'll soon learn what each word does.

Whose work is it?

Image generators are trained on huge collections of pictures from the internet, some with billions of images, including the work of artists who were never asked. Many artists say this is unfair, and in rare cases a model has made near-copies of pictures it was trained on. By 2025, courts in several countries were hearing cases about this, and the rules are still being worked out. Some companies say they train only on pictures they have permission to use. Some tools add a visible label or an invisible watermark to show that a picture was made by AI, but not all of them do, and editing can remove some marks. The most harmful use is deepfakes: never make or share a fake of a real person without their permission.

Did you know? In 2023, an AI-made picture of the Pope in a huge white puffer jacket spread around the world, and many people believed it was real. It was a harmless joke, but it showed how easily a fake can fool us. Before you share a surprising picture, ask where it comes from.

Key points

  • Generative AI learns patterns from huge numbers of examples and uses them to make new text, pictures, music, voices and videos.
  • A diffusion model starts from random noise and removes it step by step, guided by your prompt.
  • AI-made media raises real questions: artists' consent and copyright, labels and watermarks, and harmful deepfakes.

Check yourself

What does a diffusion model learn during its training?

Show the answer

Right answer: To take noise out of a picture, a little at a time

In training, a diffusion model sees pictures with noise added and learns to take the noise away, step by step. It doesn't keep its training pictures to copy them, and it doesn't search the internet: it builds a new picture out of random noise, guided by the prompt.
